en: Taal Volcano features a main crater situated on an island located inside a lake that fills the caldera of a larger ancient volcano.
The island of Mindanao is home to the Philippine eagle, the world's largest eagle, which can have a wingspan of up to two meters.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features a navigable underground waterway that flows directly into the sea, meaning its lower portion experiences daily tidal changes.
The Cordillera Mountain Range contains the Banaue Rice Terraces, which were carved into the mountains by the Ifugao people over 2,000 years ago using hand tools.
The city of Baguio experiences a significantly cooler climate than the rest of the Philippines because it is situated at an elevation of 1,500 meters.
The Philippine species Rafflesia schadenbergiana produces massive flowers up to one meter across, making it one of the largest individual blooms in the entire world.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea protects over 600 species of fish and 360 species of coral within its pristine UNESCO World Heritage marine area.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 cone-shaped hills that turn brown during the dry season, resembling giant chocolate kisses.
The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo injected sulfur dioxide into the stratosphere, temporarily lowering the Earth's average global temperature by about half a degree Celsius.
The Agusan Marsh Wildlife Sanctuary in Mindanao is the largest freshwater swamp in the Philippines, storing massive amounts of water for crocodiles and migratory birds.
The Philippines holds among the world's largest nickel reserves, primarily mined in Surigao del Norte and widely used to manufacture stainless steel and batteries.
The tamaraw, a small, V-horned buffalo, is entirely endemic to Mindoro and is critically endangered, with a wild population of fewer than 500 individuals.
